newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss Re sees M&G on books at year-end.
newsitem.headline: Swiss Re sees M&G on books at year-end.

text.p: Reinsurance giant Swiss Re welcomed European Commission approval on Monday for the purchase of Mercantile & General Reinsurance Co as a step towards consolidating the British firm on its end-1996 balance sheet.

"We hope to have approval from all the necessary regulatory agencies by early December so that we consolidate M&G on our balance sheet for this year," a spokesman for Swiss Reinsurance Co told Reuters.

The European Commission earlier said it had approved the purchase of M&G from Britain's Prudential Group because it would not give Swiss Re a dominant position in the European Union reinsurance market.
Permission for the August deal is still needed from regulators in countries including the United States, Canada and Australia, the spokesman said.

Swiss Re, the world's second biggest reinsurance group after Munich Re of Germany, last week said it would not consolidate M&G earnings until next year but hoped to add the new group to its balance sheet as of December 31.
The deal will reinforce Swiss Re's dominance in the global life market, although the European Commission ruled it would still have less than 15 percent of the overall EU reinsurance market.

It brings in M&G's strong U.K. and U.S. portfolios and three main product lines -- life, health-related and general reinsurance -- with the bulk of premium income and profit generated by long-term business.
